title: Tracking the Intangible: Quantifying Effort in NFL Running Backs
text: The saying “giving your ‘100%’” is quite common, but what does that exactly mean? This project attempted to quantify this effort for NFL running backs. For each running back and utilizing Big Data Bowl tracking data, we graphed acceleration-speed (A-S) profiles. Using quantitative generalized additive modeling (QGAM), we found the highest percentiles of acceleration for each given speed. Effort is then defined by how often and close a player comes to this threshold. We also expanded this analysis to wide receivers. For more results and information, please watch the video attached!

title: Duquesne Light Company
text: During the summer of 2026, I was an Operations Analytics intern at Duquesne Light Company (DLC), an electrical utilities company powering Pittsburgh and neighboring areas. My intern team and I conducted an analysis to evaluate the efficiency and data completeness of planned outages. Planned outages are known outages, where DLC calls customers and companies in advance. To measure efficiency, we calculated how well DLC estimates duration and the average difference between the planned start time vs. the actual start time. For data completeness, we examined how many missing values were in the outage management system. Some of these values include start and end times, crew assignments, and coordinates. We then presented our findings to some members of the executive leadership team.

title: Clustering MLB hitters based off their two-strike approaches
text:
This project utilized k-means clustering to group MLB players by their two-strike approaches. MLB Savant released new bat tracking data for the 2024 season, like bat speed and swing length, which makes this project possible. It’s a common belief to take a two-strike approach (prioritizing contact and reducing bat speed) in baseball, but is this true in the MLB?
For clustering, I selected three variables: bat speed, two-strike xWOBA, and strikeout percentage. Using the elbow method, I found that 5 clusters was ideal. At the bottom of the poster, I also included median statistical measures for each cluster, adding in swing length and barrel percentage. Overall, the model segmented two-strike hitters into five groups: poor, power, contact, better contact, and average two-strike hitters. Pitchers can take this analysis and better plan when facing certain batters, based on their two-strike hitting abilities.
I presented this project at the 5th Annual Ohio State Sports Analytics Conference and won the award for “Outstanding Sports Analytics for Professional Sports.” The poster is attached!

title: Cleveland Cavaliers Hackathon 2024
text: The Cleveland Cavaliers challenged us to segment Cavaliers’ fans based on their food, beverage, and retail purchases. Utilizing hierarchical clustering and silhouette scores, we determined three distinct fan subsets, one of which we clustered again to provide a deeper analysis. In presenting our findings through the use of data visualizations, we provided valuable insights for the Cavaliers’ Front Office. We were awarded first place for our submission. For our results and analysis, please download or view the attached PowerPoint.

title: Analyzing passing characteristics of 2023 Women’s World Cup soccer players
text:
This project focused on discovering passing insights for players and teams in the 2023 Women’s World Cup. It was also the first of two projects for the 2025 Carnegie Mellon Sports Analytics Camp (CMSACamp), where I conducted undergraduate research.
Initial EDA found that passing completion rates tend to decrease towards the end of the game. This is most likely due to fatigue and “last-ditch” scoring efforts. Essentially, teams are more desperate to score at the end of the game and will force passes. We also took at look at Spain, the eventual winners of the Women’s World Cup, and how they fared against another country in their group, Costa Rica. EDA showed that Spain dominated in the passing game to advance to the knockout rounds, while Costa Rica struggled, especially against Spain.
Finally, we performed k-means clustering to cluster players based off of their passing abilities. Utilizing the elbow method, we found 5 distinct clusters, as seen on our presentation. What may be surprising is that well-known USA winger Megan Rapinoe was clustered into the “poor” passing group. However, looking at her 2023 somewhat poor performance in the tournament justifies her placement. Feel free to look at our presentation for more results and the rest of our analysis!

title: Cleveland Cavaliers Hackathon 2025
text: The Cleveland Cavaliers tasked us to project ticket sales for games in their 25-26 NBA season based on historical sales. We created a dashboard through R Shiny to visualize this projection and help decision makers know if games were on pace with their ticket sales. Our submission earned us first place in the event! Check out our full presentation!
